propositions.text: The appellant is a Haitian citizen appealing a negative RPD decision from 2020.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (Appellant), a citizen of Haiti, is appealing the negative decision rendered in his claim by the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) on XXXX XXXX, 2020.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant, a Haitian citizen, appeals the RPD's negative 2020 decision.

propositions.text: The RPD found the appellant not credible on allegations of gang threats, attacks, complaints, and threats to his wife in 2017-2018.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellant was not credible in his allegations that he was targeted and threatened by gang members in XXXX 2017 after failing to provide a payment out of a group savings plan with other merchants; that his home and car were shot at and his home ransacked in XXXX 2017; that he made complaints to authorities regarding these events; and that his wife was threatened by the gang in XXXX2017 and XXXX2018.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the appellant not credible on his 2017-2018 gang-related allegations.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD erred by microscopic analysis in negative credibility findings.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD erred in its negative credibility findings that resulted from a microscopic analysis.

propositions.text: The appellant alleges RPD bias and improper admission of an exhibit he did not want to produce, violating fundamental justice.
propositions.quote: The Appellant also argues that there was a violation of the fundamental principles of justice, as the RPD demonstrated bias and entered into evidence an exhibit that the Appellant did not wish to produce.

propositions.text: The appellant submits the RPD erred by failing to analyze s97, state protection, or internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the RPD erred in failing to conduct an analysis under s97, state protection or internal flight alternative.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred in credibility, bias, evidence admission, and s97/state protection/IFA analysis.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in negative credibility findings.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD erred in its negative credibility findings.

propositions.text: No evidence of RPD bias; appellant did not indicate objection to exhibit during hearing.
propositions.quote: I do not find that there was evidence of bias on the part of the RPD and noted that the Appellant did not provide any indication during the RPD hearing that he did not wish to enter the particular exhibit into evidence.

propositions.text: No violation of procedural fairness found.
propositions.quote: I therefore do not find that there was a violation of procedural fairness.

propositions.text: RPD erred in not analyzing s97, state protection, or internal flight alternative due to credibility error.
propositions.quote: As the RPD erred in its credibility findings, I find that it also erred in not conducting an analysis under s97, state protection or internal flight alternative (IFA).

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD erred on credibility and s97 analysis but no bias or procedural fairness violation.

propositions.text: Appellant produced credible evidence of personal risk to life under s97(1)(b) IRPA on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant has produced credible evidence that, on the balance of probabilities, he faces a risk to life that is personal and one that is not generally faced by others in Haiti in accordance with section 97(1)(b) of Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA);

propositions.text: Appellant rebutted presumption of adequate state protection in Haiti.
propositions.quote: that he has rebutted the presumption of adequate state protection in Haiti;

propositions.text: No viable internal flight alternative exists for appellant in Haiti.
propositions.quote: and that there is no viable internal flight alternative for the Appellant in Haiti.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant credible, facing personal risk, rebutting state protection, and lacking internal flight alternative.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed; appellant is a person in need of protection under s97(1)(b) IRPA.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed. I substitute my own decision that the Appellant is a "person in need of protection" in accordance with section 97(1)(b) of IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The appeal is allowed; appellant recognized as person in need of protection under s97(1)(b).

propositions.text: No new evidence or oral hearing request was provided to RAD.
propositions.quote: No new evidence has been provided to the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) and there has been no request for an oral hearing.

paragraphs.summary: No new evidence or oral hearing request was provided to RAD.

propositions.text: The RAD independently assessed evidence including audio and transcript to determine RPD errors of law, fact, or mixed law and fact.
propositions.quote: When reviewing the RPD decision, I independently assessed the evidence, including listening to the audio recording of the RPD hearing of February 11, 2020, and reviewing the transcript, to determine whether or not the RPD was correct in relation to each alleged error of law, of fact, or of mixed law and fact.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD independently assessed evidence and RPD errors of law, fact, or mixed law and fact.

propositions.text: The appellant's allegations do not raise Convention grounds; analysis proceeds under s97 IRPA.
propositions.quote: As the allegations of the Appellant do not give rise to Convention grounds, I shall examine the allegations in light of s 97 of IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant's allegations lack Convention grounds; analysis is under s97 IRPA.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's credibility undermined by date discrepancy in complaint document and testimony about complaint preparation date in 2017.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellant's credibility was undermined by the difference between the date on which he alleged that he had prepared a complaint with his lawyer regarding the threats received by a gang leader on XXXX XXXX, 2017, which he testified had been the same day, and the information in the complaint filed with authorities1, which indicated that the complaint had been prepared on XXXX XXXX, 2017.

propositions.text: Appellant testified he was out of country on complaint date; suggested administrative error or delivery date explanation.
propositions.quote: Although the complaint was dated and signed on XXXX XXXX, 2017 regarding the XXXX XXXX, 2017 incident, the Appellant had testified that he had been out of the country on that date, as was indicated in his passport, and said that maybe the date had been an administrative error, or that maybe it represented the date it had been delivered to the magistrate.

propositions.text: RPD was not satisfied; document appeared signed on date but margin notations and stamp indicated receipt on that date.
propositions.quote: The RPD was not satisfied by the explanation of the Appellant, as the document appeared to have been signed by the Appellant and his lawyer on the date of XXXX XXXX, 2017, but notations in the margin indicated that it was received on that date and a stamp on the document also bears that date.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's credibility undermined on 2017 incident and gave no weight to document.
propositions.quote: The RPD therefore found that the credibility of the Appellant was undermined regarding the alleged XXXX XXXX, 2017 incident and awarded no weight to the document.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's credibility undermined by date discrepancy in complaint document and testimony, giving no weight to the document.

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD erred by not allowing opportunity to explain date contradiction during hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that this is a contradiction that he cannot explain, but argues that the RPD erred in not giving him the opportunity to provide an explanation during the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred by not allowing explanation opportunity for date contradiction.

propositions.text: RPD did ask appellant about date discrepancy; appellant explained possible magistrate or administrative error.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD did not err in failing to give the Appellant the opportunity to explain during the hearing, because it did do so, clearly asking the Appellant why the document indicated the date of XXXX XXXXwhen the Appellant had testified that the complaint had been signed on the XXXX, and the Appellant answered that maybe it was a mistake of the magistrate or an administrative error, because he had been in the U.S on that date2.

propositions.text: RPD erred in giving no weight to the document and finding appellant's credibility undermined by this contradiction.
propositions.quote: However, I find that the RPD did err in giving the document no weight and in finding that the Appellant's credibility was undermined by this contradiction.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD asked about date discrepancy but erred in giving no weight to document and undermining credibility.

propositions.text: The complaint document is detailed, corroborated by testimony and BOC, and includes identifying info, threats, and legal references.
propositions.quote: The document in question, a complaint prepared by the Appellant's lawyer and then registered with a magistrate, is extremely detailed and provides information that is corroborated by both testimony and the Basis of Claim Form (BOC). It includes identifying information about the Appellant, his lawyer, the prosecutor's office that received the complaint, the circumstances that led to the threats of the Appellant by the gang leader, a quotation in Creole (for which translation was provided) of the threat by the gang leader to the Appellant, as well as a reference to the specific legislative provisions that are applicable regarding the threats.

paragraphs.summary: The complaint document is detailed and corroborated by testimony and BOC, including threats and legal references.

propositions.text: The date discrepancy is minor and appellant immediately explained it; it should not outweigh detailed corroborated info.
propositions.quote: I consider that this one element of the date of the document, which differs by a matter of days from that testified to by the Appellant-who immediately said that he could not have signed on that date of XXXX XXXXbecause he was out of the country, as corroborated by his passport-and who did not try to embellish or invent an answer but spontaneously provided testimony, should not outweigh the detailed information provided in the document or in the BOC narrative or testimony.

propositions.text: The document merits weight; unexplained date discrepancy should not undermine appellant's credibility.
propositions.quote: I find that the document merits weight in establishing the Appellant's allegations, and the unexplained discrepancy of the date should not undermine his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the minor date discrepancy should not undermine credibility; the document merits weight.

propositions.text: RPD gave no weight to documents D-5 and D-6 about XXXX XXXX, 2017 incident and found no link to gang threats.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that documents D-5 and D-6, which were complaints regarding the alleged incident of XXXX XXXX, 2017, merited no weight, and that the Appellant had not established that this incident had a link with the alleged threats against him by the gang leader, for the reasons as set out below.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD gave no weight to documents about the 2017 incident and found no link to gang threats.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD used microscopic examination and circular reasoning to reject allegations and documents, thus erred.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD undertook a microscopic examination of the differences between the documents and the information in the BOC and testimony in reaching a negative credibility finding, and used circular reasoning to reject the allegations because it had rejected the documents; therefore the RPD erred.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred by microscopic examination and circular reasoning rejecting allegations and documents.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in giving no weight to documents and negative credibility finding on link to gang threats.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD erred in awarding no weight to the documents and in reaching a negative credibility finding concerning the link of this event to the threats against the Appellant by the gang leader, for the reasons as set out below.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD erred in giving no weight to documents and negative credibility on gang threat link.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's credibility mitigated by different terminology in BOC and testimony describing 2017 incident.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the credibility of the Appellant was mitigated by what it saw as different terminology used to describe the same incident in the BOC versus that which was used during the Appellant's testimony.

propositions.text: RPD noted BOC used 'fouiller' and testimony used 'saccager' to describe gang actions in appellant's house.
propositions.quote: The RPD considered that the use of the word "fouiller" to describe the actions of the gang members in the Appellant's house on XXXX XXXX, 2017 when describing the incident in his BOC, was different from the word "saccager" used during his testimony to describe the actions by the gang members in his house.

propositions.text: RPD asked why BOC said house was searched but testimony said items destroyed; appellant said words meant same.
propositions.quote: The RPD asked the Appellant why he had only alleged in his BOC that his house had been searched by the bandits, without mentioning specifically that anything had been destroyed, but that during his testimony he had said that the bandits had destroyed some of the items in his house. The Appellant replied that the word he used in his BOC, "fouiller" meant the same thing as "saccager" and implied that the bandits had caused damage inside the house.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's explanation unsatisfactory and concluded credibility was undermined.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that this explanation was not satisfactory and concluded that the Appellant's credibility was undermined as a result.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's credibility undermined by differing terminology for 2017 incident despite appellant's explanation.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred by not considering cultural, language, interpreter, and dictionary factors in credibility assessment.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that when evaluating the credibility of a claimant, different factors that can affect testimony should be taken into consideration and the RPD erred in failing to do so. The Appellant submits that cultural differences, differences in language expressions, use of synonyms, the fact that an interpreter from Creole to French was used both at the hearing and in writing the BOC narrative, should all be taken into consideration in this situation, as well as the dictionary definitions of the words in question, when assessing the credibility of the Appellant for the apparent differences in the words used. The Appellant submits that the dictionary definitions of the words "saccager" and "fouiller" are not contradictory because "fouiller" means to search while creating disorder and not caring if damage is caused, while "saccager" means to destroy.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred by ignoring cultural, language, interpreter, and dictionary factors in credibility.

propositions.text: RPD erred in considering different words undermined credibility; words are similar in meaning.
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD erred in considering that the use of different words by the Appellant to describe the XXXX XXXX, 2017 incident undermined his credibility, as I find that the words themselves are very similar.

propositions.text: Considering interpreter and translation context, words are synonymous and not contradictory.
propositions.quote: When I additionally consider that the Appellant was assisted by a Creole-French interpreter at the hearing and in his BOC, such that the words used are being translated from one language to another and the Appellant's use of words must be considered in that context, I agree with the submissions of the Appellant in this regard.

propositions.text: Appellant explained 'fouiller' meant searching causing disorder and damage; 'saccager' means destroy; meanings close enough not to contradict.
propositions.quote: During the hearing, the RPD asked the Appellant to explain why in the BOC it said that the bandits had "fouillé" his house but during his testimony, he had said that they had damaged items in the house, and he replied that it was the same thing, as he was referring to the bandits searching through his home, taking what they wanted and causing damage3. I consider the words to be synonymous and find that the RPD erred in considering that these were of such a difference as to be contradictory and undermine the Appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: Appellant's credibility regarding 2017 incident is not undermined by word differences.
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant's credibility regarding the allegations of XXXX XXXX, 2017 is not undermined as a result.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD erred in considering word differences undermined credibility; words are synonymous and credibility is intact.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant's credibility undermined by contradictions about seeing agents of harm on XXXX XXXX, 2017
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the credibility of the Appellant was undermined by the differences in his testimony regarding his observations of the agents of harm on XXXX XXXX, 2017.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant first said he saw people but did not recognize them, later said no electricity and nothing could be seen
propositions.quote: The RPD considered that the Appellant had indicated originally that he had seen people, but did not recognize them, but later in his testimony had said that there was no electricity and that nothing could be seen.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant gave no reasonable explanation for contradiction, so did not prove break-in was orchestrated by gang leader
propositions.quote: The RPD found that because the Appellant had not provided a reasonable explanation for this contradiction, he did not establish on the balance of probabilities that the break-in to his house on XXXX XXXX, 2017 had been orchestrated by the particular alleged gang leader.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's credibility undermined by contradictory testimony about seeing agents of harm and lack of reasonable explanation for break-in orchestration.

propositions.text: Appellant argues no electricity meant he could not clearly see people but some natural light allowed seeing something, so no contradiction
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the fact that there was no electricity meant that he could not clearly see people in the house, but there would still have been some natural illumination from the stars and moon, such that he was able to see something.

propositions.text: Appellant submits he proved on balance of probabilities that break-in was orchestrated by gang leader due to prior threats and timing of payment
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the Appellant submits that even though he could not clearly see the individuals in his house, it was established that on the balance of probabilities, it was an action orchestrated by the gang leader, as he had no problems prior to the threats by the gang leader to extort a portion of the balance owing from his group savings with the other merchants, and the gang leader had specifically made reference to the upcoming payment that the Appellant was expecting, following which his house was broken into the night he received the payment.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues no contradiction in testimony about seeing people and submits he proved break-in orchestration by gang leader on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Appellant's BOC said he hid behind bush and saw unknown men inside his house during incident
propositions.quote: In his BOC, the Appellant indicated that during the incident, he had left from the back of his house and hidden behind a bush in his neighbour's yard, during which time he saw men that he did not know inside his house.

propositions.text: RPD confronted Appellant about earlier testimony saying he hadn't seen men before complaint and gang leader ID
propositions.quote: During his testimony, the RPD confronted the Appellant with the fact that earlier in his testimony, he had said that he hadn't seen the men prior to making a complaint against them and identifying the gang leader in his complaint.

propositions.text: Appellant replied it was impossible to identify men due to late night and power outage in Haiti
propositions.quote: The Appellant replied that it was impossible to identify the men in his house because it was late at night and in Haiti at that time there was a power outage.

propositions.text: No contradiction found; RPD erred in impugning credibility on this basis
propositions.quote: I do not find that there is any contradiction, and I find that the RPD erred in considering that this impugned his credibility.

propositions.text: Whether Appellant saw men a little or not at all, he did not recognize them; accusation based on threats, not visual ID
propositions.quote: because whether or not the Appellant saw the men who broke into his house a little bit or not at all, either way he did not recognize them, and his reason for accusing the gang leader was not based on his visual observation during the incident but on the fact that unknown people had broken into his home and threatened him, after firing gunshots.

propositions.text: Appellant's BOC said bandit addressed him by first name and threatened to find him
propositions.quote: In the Appellant's BOC, he had written that one of the bandits had addressed him by his first name and said that he could hide, but that they would find him.

propositions.text: Appellant met balance of probabilities standard that break-in was connected to gang leader's threats and timing of payment
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant has met his standard of proof of the balance of probabilities, with respect to the identity of the individuals who broke into his house, shot outside his house and threatened him on XXXX XXXX, 2017, based on the previous threats by the gang leader and the fact that the break-in occurred when he was expected to receive his money.

propositions.text: Given credible evidence, more probable than not that break-in was connected to gang leader's threats; RPD erred in contrary finding
propositions.quote: I consider that, given the credible evidence provided by the Appellant, it is more probable than not that the individuals who broke into his house were there in connection with the gang leader's threats, and I therefore find that the RPD erred in finding that the break-in had not been orchestrated by the gang leader.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no contradiction in Appellant's testimony and that the break-in was likely orchestrated by the gang leader, reversing the RPD's finding.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant's credibility undermined by omission of theft or damage in complaint after XXXX XXXX, 2017 incident
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellant's credibility was undermined by the omission from his complaint following the alleged XXXX XXXX, 2017 incident of the theft of money from his home or the destruction of items inside his house.

propositions.text: RPD confronted Appellant about omission; Appellant said magistrate may not have noted all info and omission possible
propositions.quote: When the RPD confronted the Appellant about this omission, he replied during the hearing that the magistrate had not noted all the information and that it was possible that he had omitted that, explaining that to him it was logical that the bandits would have been looking for money if they were breaking into his house.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant's explanation unsatisfactory and omission undermined credibility as stolen money was central allegation
propositions.quote: The RPD found that this explanation was unsatisfactory and that, as the stolen money was at the heart of his allegations, its omission from the complaint with the justice of the peace and from the extract of the minutes of the clerk undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's credibility undermined by omission of theft or damage in complaint and found his explanation unsatisfactory.

propositions.text: Appellant argues complaints indicate bandits entered house to take money, equivalent to stolen money
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that even if the complaints do not specifically mention that the money was stolen, they do indicate that the bandits had entered the house to take money, "emporter l'argent", and that there is no difference between saying that they had entered the house to take money or that they had stolen money.

propositions.text: Appellant submits allegation of stolen money is in BOC narrative; RPD erred in negative credibility finding
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the Appellant submits that the allegation of the money having been stolen during the break-in is indicated in the BOC narrative. The Appellant therefore argues that the RPD erred in reaching a negative credibility finding in this regard.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues complaints and BOC show money was stolen and that the RPD erred in negative credibility finding.

propositions.text: RPD erred in negative credibility finding due to alleged omission; no omission found in documents
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD erred in making a negative credibility finding due to the apparent omission from the documents, as I do not find that there was an omission in those documents.

propositions.text: Exhibit D-5 complaint indicates bandits entered house to assassinate and steal money, expecting currency at house
propositions.quote: Exhibit D-5, which is a complaint that was prepared by the Appellant's lawyer in Haiti and addressed to a justice of the peace in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, indicates that the bandits on the night of XXXX XXXX, 2017, entered the Appellant's house to assassinate him and steal money, as they expected that he had XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in Haitian currency at the house.

propositions.text: Exhibit D-6 extract of minutes contains same info about bandits' intent to assassinate and steal money
propositions.quote: Exhibit D-6, which is an extract of the minutes of the clerk of the justice of the peace of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, contains the same information.

propositions.text: RPD confronted Appellant about complaint not mentioning bandits took money; Appellant said omission possible
propositions.quote: During the hearing, the RPD had confronted the Appellant and asked why the complaint does not really mention that the bandits had taken money, it just says that they were looking for money, and the Appellant replied that it could have happened that they had forgotten to put in everything that he had said, but that the bandits were coming to his house for a reason, it was logical that they wanted to take something.

propositions.text: BOC indicates next morning Appellant realized money was stolen
propositions.quote: In his BOC, it is indicated that the next morning, he realized that they had stolen money.

propositions.text: Information in exhibits, testimony and BOC consistent and corroborate allegations; established on balance of probabilities
propositions.quote: I consider that the information in the exhibits indicates the intention of the bandits to steal money, which combined with the testimony of the Appellant and the information in the BOC, is consistent and corroborates the allegations of the Appellant regarding the incident of XXXX XXXX, 2017, such that the allegations have been established on the balance of probabilities.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no omission in documents and that evidence consistently corroborates the Appellant's allegations about theft during the incident.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant's credibility undermined by omission in BOC of car damage allegation from complaints
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellant's credibility was adversely affected by the omission in his BOC of the allegation in the complaints that his car had sustained damage from bullets during the XXXX XXXX, 2017 incident.

propositions.text: RPD asked Appellant about omission; Appellant said it was his car and could not explain omission
propositions.quote: During the hearing, the RPD asked the Appellant about this and he replied that it was his car that was damaged and that he could not explain why he had left this out of his BOC.

propositions.text: RPD found credibility lessened by omission during testimony when Appellant said no other event besides ransacking happened
propositions.quote: Also, the RPD found that the Appellant's credibility was lessened by the omission of this during his testimony, as when he was asked if anything besides the ransacking of his house had happened during this event, he answered no.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's credibility undermined by omission of car damage in BOC and testimony and unexplained omission.

propositions.text: Appellant argues omission of car damage detail in BOC should not impugn credibility as gunshots were mentioned
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that even if the BOC did not mention that his car had been hit by bullets, he had written in the BOC that he had heard gunshots, such that the fact that the car was damaged by the gunshots was a mere detail, the omission of which should not impugn his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues omission of car damage detail in BOC is minor and should not affect credibility.

propositions.text: BOC states Appellant heard gunshots after knocks at door on XXXX XXXX, 2017
propositions.quote: In the Appellant's BOC, he wrote that on XXXX XXXX, 2017, after knocks at his door late at night, to which he did not answer, he heard gunshots.

propositions.text: Exhibit D-6 shows justice of the peace observed bullet holes in house and car, and found cartridges nearby
propositions.quote: In Exhibit D-6, the extract of the minutes of the clerk for the justice of the peace of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, it is indicated that a justice of the peace went to the home of the Appellant on XXXX XXXX, 2017 to observe and document the damage that had been sustained after the event of XXXX XXXX, 2017. Aside from noting bullet holes in the front door and wall of the house, the justice of the peace also noted that a white car, which was identified by its licence plate, manufacturer and model, had bullet holes in the front and rear windows, as well as five cartridges from bullets in the alley near the house.

propositions.text: RPD asked Appellant who owned car; Appellant said he did and used it for family
propositions.quote: During the hearing, the RPD asked the Appellant who owned the car that was mentioned in this report and the Appellant replied that he did, that he used it to drive his wife and children.

propositions.text: RPD asked why car damage not mentioned in BOC; Appellant said it was in complaint
propositions.quote: When he was asked why he had not mentioned in his BOC that the car had been shot at, he answered that it was in the complaint.

propositions.text: RPD erred in impugning credibility due to omission of car damage in BOC and testimony; allegation consistent and corroborated
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD erred in impugning his credibility due to the omission from his BOC and testimony of this information, because I consider that the allegation that the Appellant's car, which was parked near his house, would have been damaged by bullets is consistent with his allegations in his BOC and testimony that he had heard gunshots outside his house that night.

propositions.text: Justice of the peace report detailed and corroborates other allegations of that night
propositions.quote: Also, the information was documented in the report of the justice of the peace in a detailed fashion, while also corroborating the other allegations of that night.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred in impugning credibility over omission of car damage, as evidence and testimony consistently corroborate the allegation.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant's credibility undermined by omission in one complaint of info in another about wife's threats after Appellant left Haiti
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellant's credibility was undermined by the omission in one document of information that appeared in another document, regarding complaints that the Appellant's wife had made following threats by the gang leader to her, after the Appellant had left Haiti.

propositions.text: One complaint dated XXXX XXXX, 2018 says gang leader threatened wife at store and asked for Appellant
propositions.quote: In one document dated XXXX XXXX, 2018, prepared by the Appellant's lawyer in Haiti and addressed to a justice of the peace, there is a complaint that on XXXX XXXX, 2018, the gang leader threatened his wife at the store and asked for the Appellant.

propositions.text: Another complaint dated XXXX XXXX, 2018 has same info plus wife gave bandits money to leave
propositions.quote: In another document dated XXXX XXXX, 2018, prepared by the Appellant's lawyer in Haiti and addressed to the prosecutor's office, there is the same information as in the previous complaint with the additional mention that the Appellant's wife had given the bandits money so that they would leave.

propositions.text: RPD found omission of info and address inconsistency undermined credibility and probative value; found Appellant did not prove wife's threats on balance of probabilities
propositions.quote: The RPD considered that the omission of this information from one of the complaints, combined with the address on the complaints as being the Appellant's original address in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, even though he had testified that she had been in hiding in XXXX at that time, undermined the credibility of the Appellant and the probative value of the two complaints. The RPD therefore found that the Appellant had not established on the balance of probabilities that his wife had been threatened by the gang leader.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Appellant's credibility undermined by omission and address inconsistency in complaints about wife's threats, denying proof on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Appellant argues second document with extra info was not intended as evidence and RPD overemphasized minor detail from weak judicial system
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the second document with the additional information was not intended to have been put into evidence and that the RPD put too much emphasis on a small detail that was in a document from a country that is known not to have rigorous judicial writings, according to the objective documentary evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the second complaint was not evidence and the RPD overemphasized a minor detail from a weak judicial system.

propositions.text: RPD erred in negative credibility finding about wife's threats based on address and addition of one element
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD erred in reaching a negative credibility finding regarding the allegation of threats against the Appellant's wife based on the address of the documents and the addition of one element in one of the reports.

propositions.text: Testimony, BOC and forms show wife was hiding with children elsewhere and family owns house but no longer occupy it
propositions.quote: I consider that the testimony of the Appellant, his BOC and the forms he filled out all indicate that his wife was hiding with the children in another location, that they owned the house in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXbut that they no longer occupy it, and I find that this outweighs the fact that her address in the complaints was indicated as being the official family residence in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Addition of allegation wife gave money to gang leader is peripheral and omission from one document is not a credibility concern
propositions.quote: Furthermore, I consider the addition of the allegation that the Appellant's wife had provided money to the gang leader so that they would leave the store as being peripheral and its omission from one document not a credibility concern.

propositions.text: Documents have weight for allegation wife was threatened and gang leader still looking for Appellant after he left Haiti
propositions.quote: I find that these documents have weight for the allegation that the Appellant's wife was threatened and that the gang leader was still looking for the Appellant after he had left Haiti.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD erred in negative credibility finding about wife's threats and finds the documents credible and weighty.

propositions.text: RPD did not discuss detailed info in Exhibits D-5, D-6, D-7 except omissions; exhibits merit high weight in establishing Appellant's allegations
propositions.quote: The RPD decision did not discuss the detailed information contained in Exhibits D-5, D-6 and D-7, except to point out the omissions that they either contained or that they represented in the Appellant's testimony. However, I find that after reviewing them carefully, they merit high weight in establishing the allegations of the Appellant, as they contain many specific, identifying details about the Appellant, the lawyers who prepared the complaints, the observations of the Appellant, his wife, and a justice of the peace regarding the various incidents, including contact information and relevant legislative provisions of the various offences.

propositions.text: Exhibit D-11 letter from Appellant's lawyer says file still open but no follow-up by judicial authorities as of Feb 2020
propositions.quote: Exhibit D-11 is a letter from the Appellant's lawyer in Haiti that indicates that his file is still open, but that as of February 2020, no follow-up has been made by the judicial authorities.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the exhibits merit high weight in establishing allegations and notes lawyer's letter about no judicial follow-up.

propositions.text: Appellant is credible and proved on balance of probabilities he was targeted by gang members after refusing payment and threats
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant is credible and has established, on the balance of probabilities, that he was targeted by gang members after failing to provide a payment out of a group savings plan with other merchants, which the gang leader had threatened him to provide on XXXX XXXX, 2017; that he made a complaint to authorities regarding this threat; that on XXXX XXXX, 2017, after receiving the payment in question, gunshots were fired at his home and at his car, his home was broken into and ransacked, and money was stolen by unidentified individuals that he has established on the balance of probabilities were connected to the gang leader who had threatened him; that he made another complaint to authorities regarding this incident; that subsequently he went into hiding; that in XXXX XXXX XXXX 2017, his wife was threatened by the same gang leader at the store who said that he would find the Appellant; that after the Appellant left Haiti, his wife was again threatened by the gang leader in XXXX 2018; that as of XXXX 2020, the lawyer of the Appellant in Haiti indicated that the file is still open but that no further legal action has been taken regarding his complaints.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant credible and proved on balance of probabilities he was targeted by gang members and threats extended to his wife.

propositions.text: Based on credible evidence and objective documents, Appellant faces personal risk to life from gang members due to refusal to pay and reporting threats
propositions.quote: Based on the credible evidence provided by the Appellant regarding the existence of the agents of harm, the fact that they have targeted him and threatened his wife recently, and the objective documentary evidence that indicates that gang members take vengeance for reporting them to police and that they commonly target family members of those who have wronged them, I therefore find that the Appellant faces, on the balance of probabilities, a risk to his life that is personal and one that is not generally faced by others, as he has been particularly targeted by gang members who have tried to take vengeance against him because he had refused to provide them with payment and had contacted the authorities through his lawyer to report that he had been threatened by a gang leader, then had his home shot at and ransacked, money stolen, received further threats and did further reporting to authorities, and recent threats were made to his wife.

propositions.text: Gunshots fired at home and car, repeated personal threats and reporting indicate serious, dangerous, repeated personal targeting and risk not generally faced by others
propositions.quote: The fact that gunshots were fired at his home and his car, followed by repeated threats directed at him personally and his repeatedly reporting the agent of harm to the authorities indicates the serious and dangerous nature of the threats and their repeated and personal targeting of the Appellant, such that I find this is a risk that is not generally faced by others in Haiti.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant faces a personal, serious, repeated risk to life from gang members not generally faced by others.

propositions.text: Objective evidence shows gangs commit revenge acts for collaborating with police; those reporting are particularly targeted
propositions.quote: The objective documentary evidence shows that acts of revenge may be committed by gangs for collaborating with police, with one source reporting that those who report criminals to the police are "particularly targeted".

propositions.text: Assistant professor indicates severity and likelihood of revenge reduce over time with distance and gang power
propositions.quote: While one assistant professor indicates that the severity and likelihood of an act of revenge reduce over time, in relation to the distance from and power of a particular gang.

propositions.text: Standard of proof for risk to Appellant's life met on balance of probabilities given repeated threats and shootings over years
propositions.quote: I find that the standard of proof for a risk to the Appellant's life is met, on a balance of probabilities, based on the number of incidents in which he and his wife were threatened, the seriousness of the act of the agents of harm having shot multiple times at the Appellant's house and car, and the fact that the incidents had taken place repeatedly over the years.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds objective evidence supports risk of revenge by gangs and that the standard of proof for risk to Appellant's life is met.

propositions.text: Appellant established on balance of probabilities a personal risk to life not generally faced by others if returned to Haiti under s 97(1) IRPA
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant has established, on the balance of probabilities, that he faces a risk to life that is personal, and one that is not generally faced by others, if he were to return to Haiti, in accordance with s 97(1) of IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant established a personal risk to life not generally faced by others if returned to Haiti under s 97(1) IRPA.

propositions.text: Appellant provided credible evidence he sought help from authorities after threats and shootings but continues to be targeted with no police action
propositions.quote: The Appellant has provided credible evidence that he sought the help of authorities after he was threatened by a gang leader, then again when his house was shot at, then again by his wife after she was threatened, but that he continues to be targeted and that no action has been taken by police.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant provided credible evidence he sought help from authorities but remains targeted and police took no action.

propositions.text: Country conditions show Haitian police lack personnel and resources to protect population
propositions.quote: Specifically, country conditions indicate that the Haitian police force does not have enough personnel or resources to meet the requirements of the population.

propositions.text: Police described as incapable of defending against organized or informal crime
propositions.quote: Police are described as being incapable of defending the population against organized or informal crime.

propositions.text: Police abuses tend to go unpunished
propositions.quote: Furthermore, abuses by police tend to go unpunished.

propositions.text: Justice system described as ineffective and corrupt; high-ranking security officials linked to organized crime
propositions.quote: In addition, the justice system has been described as ineffective and corrupt, and country conditions indicate that high-ranking security officials have links to organized crime.

paragraphs.summary: Country conditions show Haitian police lack resources, are ineffective, abuses go unpunished, and justice system is corrupt with links to organized crime.

propositions.text: Appellant rebutted presumption of adequate state protection with clear and convincing evidence that Haitian authorities would be unwilling or unable to provide protection
propositions.quote: After assessing the personal and objective documentary evidence of the Appellant, I find that he has rebutted the presumption of adequate state protection with clear and convincing evidence, that if he were to seek state protection, the authorities of Haiti would be unwilling or unable to provide it.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Appellant rebutted presumption of adequate state protection with clear and convincing evidence of unwillingness or inability of Haitian authorities.

propositions.text: The agents of harm threatened him, shot at his home, and threatened his wife over several years.
propositions.quote: The Appellant provided credible evidence that the agents of harm had threatened him and shot at his home, then continued to threaten his wife after he left Haiti, over several years.

propositions.text: His wife and children live in hiding to avoid the agent of harm.
propositions.quote: he testified that his wife and children have been forced to live in hiding and that it is only because they are in hiding that the agent of harm has not found them

propositions.text: Haiti is small and impoverished; gang leader could easily pay for information about his whereabouts if he relocated.
propositions.quote: Haiti is a small and impoverished country, such that for a small amount of money the gang leader could easily obtain information about his whereabouts, in exchange for payment, if he were to try to relocate

propositions.text: If he relocated to Cap Haitien, the agent of harm would find him within weeks; nowhere in Haiti is safe to relocate.
propositions.quote: He estimated that if he were to try to relocate to Cap Haitien for example, the agent of harm would likely be able to find him within a matter of weeks, such that there is nowhere in Haiti that he could safely relocate

propositions.text: The agent of harm has connections in various towns and does not work alone.
propositions.quote: the agent of harm has connections in various towns in Haiti, that he does not work alone

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, agents of harm have means and motivation to find appellant throughout Haiti; no safe relocation possible.
propositions.quote: I find that, on the balance of probabilities, given the credible testimony by the Appellant regarding the ability and interest of the agents of harm to track him down in Haiti, specifically the repeated threats over the years to the Appellant's wife and the gang leader's connections; combined with the lack of adequate state protection in Haiti for the Appellant; that the agents of harm would have the means and motivation to find the Appellant throughout Haiti and that, as a result, there is nowhere in Haiti that would be safe for him to relocate.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant testified to ongoing threats and inability to safely relocate in Haiti; the court finds agents of harm can find him anywhere in Haiti.

propositions.text: Appellant faces a personal risk to life on balance of probabilities if returned to Haiti.
propositions.quote: I find that the Appellant has established that on the balance of probabilities, he faces a risk to life that is personal and one that is not generally faced by others, should he return to Haiti.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant faces a personal risk to life if returned to Haiti.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed, RPD decision set aside, appellant is a person in need of protection under s 97(1)(b) IRPA.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed. The RPD decision is set aside. I substitute my own decision that the Appellant is a "person in need of protection" in accordance with s 97 (1)(b) of IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal, sets aside the RPD decision, and finds the appellant a person in need of protection under IRPA.
